Brackish water is the mixture of seawater and freshwater in estuaries.
Salinity is the amount of salt in water.
Temperature is the hotness or coldness of water and changes with tides and sunlight.
Waves are movements of the water surface that organisms must withstand.

Mangroves and blue crabs are adapted to constantly changing salinity in estuaries.

Soil type in estuaries varies with wave strength and the kinds of rocks present.
Salt in estuarine soil can make the soil acidic and affect plant survival.
